```{r themes-and-palettes, include=FALSE}
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
      axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "right"
```

```{r load-data, include=FALSE}
# Load SCFA and microbiome data following the logic in the source Rmd files,
# but with paths relative to the project root (one level up from this Rmd).

## SCFA: metadata and quantification data ---------------------------------

scfa_metadata <- NULL
scfa_sample_data_long <- NULL
scfa_sample_data_long_factored <- NULL

tryCatch({
  map1 <- read_excel(
    file.path("..", "scfa_metabolomics", "metadata", "SEED LAB HMM Submission Sheet 202405.xlsx"),
    skip = 9
  ) %>%
    clean_names()
  
  colnames(map1) <- c(
    "sampleid", "group", "bile_acids_panel", "pfbbr_scfa_panel",
    "tryp_indole_panel", "tms_panel_1", "tms_panel_2", "tms_panel_3",
    "untargeted_panel", "custom_targeted_panel", "low_abundant_metabolite_panel",
    "sample_origin", "sample_type", "mouse_number",
    "services_requested_per_sample", "mouse_strain", "mouse_flora",
    "volume_ul", "sample_weight_mg", "experiment_treatment"
  )
  
  map1 <- map1 %>%
    filter(!is.na(sampleid), sampleid != "") %>%
    slice(-(1:3))
  
  map2 <- read_excel(
    file.path("..", "scfa_metabolomics", "metadata", "PS2720_xtra_samples_HMM Submission Sheet.xlsx"),
    skip = 9
  ) %>%
    clean_names()

  colnames(map2) <- colnames(map1)

  map2 <- map2 %>%
    filter(!is.na(sampleid), sampleid != "") %>%
    slice(-(1:3))

  scfa_metadata_raw <- bind_rows(map1, map2)

  conflicting_group_labels <- scfa_metadata_raw %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(sampleid), !is.na(group)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(group = stringr::str_to_lower(group)) %>%
    dplyr::count(sampleid, group) %>%
    dplyr::count(sampleid, name = "n_group_labels") %>%
    dplyr::filter(n_group_labels > 1)

  if (nrow(conflicting_group_labels) > 0) {
    stop("At least one SCFA sample ID maps to multiple obesity groups.")
  }

  # Some samples occur in both submission workbooks. Retain one metadata row
  # per sample before joining to the concentration export.
  scfa_metadata_raw <- scfa_metadata_raw %>%
    dplyr::distinct(sampleid, .keep_all = TRUE)
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Error reading SCFA metadata files: ", e$message)
})

scfa_metadata <- scfa_metadata_raw %>%
  mutate(
    # Numeric ID = independent person. A/B = sample aliquot splits of that person.
    subject = str_extract(sampleid, "^[0-9]+"),
    donor_id = subject,
    aliquot = str_to_upper(str_match(sampleid, "^[0-9]+([A-Za-z])")[, 2]),
    # Kept for sample-level joins to microbiome labels such as 84B.
    aliquot_label = paste0(subject, aliquot),
    carb_repeat = str_extract(sampleid, "(?<= )[rs]\\d|nc(?= )"),
    carbohydrate_type = case_when(
      str_detect(carb_repeat, "^r") ~ "rapid_digestible",
      str_detect(carb_repeat, "^s") ~ "slow_digestible",
      str_detect(carb_repeat, "^nc") ~ "no_carbohydrate",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    # R1/R2 and S1/S2 are biological culture wells within each A/B aliquot.
    well_repeat = if_else(
      str_detect(carb_repeat, "^nc"),
      1L,
      as.integer(str_extract(carb_repeat, "\\d+"))
    ),
    timepoint_hr = as.integer(str_extract(sampleid, "(?<= )\\d+(?=h$)")),
    aliquot_id = interaction(subject, aliquot, drop = TRUE),
    well_id = interaction(
      subject,
      aliquot,
      carbohydrate_type,
      well_repeat,
      drop = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    sampleid, group, subject, aliquot, aliquot_label, aliquot_id,
    carbohydrate_type, well_repeat, well_id, timepoint_hr
  ) %>%
  mutate(group = tolower(group)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(group), !is.na(subject), !is.na(aliquot))

tryCatch({
  scfa_raw <- fread(
    file.path("..", "scfa_metabolomics", "data", "removed_qcs_quant_results_20250722_PFBBr_PS2720_20250731.csv")
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Error reading SCFA data file: ", e$message)
})

scfa_sample_data <- left_join(scfa_metadata, scfa_raw, by = "sampleid") %>%
  mutate(group = tolower(group)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(group))

scfa_analytes <- c("acetate", "butyrate", "propionate", "5aminovalerate", "succinate")

scfa_sample_data_long <- scfa_sample_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(scfa_analytes),
    names_to = "analyte",
    values_to = "concentration"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(concentration)) %>%
  mutate(
    group_label = factor(str_to_title(group), levels = c("Control", "Case")),
    carbohydrate_type_label = str_replace_all(carbohydrate_type, "_", " ") %>%
      str_to_title()
  )

scfa_sample_data_long_factored <- scfa_sample_data_long %>%
  mutate(
    group = factor(group, levels = c("control", "case")),
    carbohydrate_type = factor(
      carbohydrate_type,
      levels = c("no_carbohydrate", "rapid_digestible", "slow_digestible")
    ),
    timepoint_hr = factor(timepoint_hr),
    subject = factor(subject),
    aliquot_id = factor(aliquot_id),
    well_id = factor(well_id)
  )

## Microbiome: metadata, phyloseq, and relative abundances --------------

micro_metadata <- NULL
ps <- NULL
ps_rel <- NULL

tryCatch({
  micro_metadata_raw <- readr::read_tsv(
    file.path(
      "..", "microbiome_analysis", "zr24558.16S_250813.zymo",
      "00...AllSamples.Bac16Sv34", "Sample_Information", "sample.metadata.csv"
    ),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  ) %>%
    janitor::clean_names()
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Error reading microbiome metadata file: ", e$message)
})

micro_metadata <- micro_metadata_raw %>%
  # Clean up double dots in labels like "NC..48H" and trim whitespace
  dplyr::mutate(
    customer_label = stringr::str_replace_all(customer_label, "\\.\\.", "."),
    customer_label = stringr::str_trim(customer_label)
  ) %>%
  separate(
    customer_label,
    into = c("aliquot_id", "replicate_code", "timepoint"),
    sep = "\\.",
    remove = FALSE
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Numeric donor is the independent person; A/B aliquot is nested within donor.
    aliquot_id = stringr::str_to_upper(aliquot_id),
    donor_id = stringr::str_extract(aliquot_id, "^[0-9]+"),
    # Legacy alias: subject_id previously meant the A/B label.
    subject_id = aliquot_id,
    carbohydrate = case_when(
      stringr::str_detect(replicate_code, "R") ~ "RDC",
      stringr::str_detect(replicate_code, "S") ~ "SDC",
      TRUE ~ "No Added Carb"
    ),
    carbohydrate = factor(carbohydrate, levels = c("No Added Carb", "RDC", "SDC")),
    timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = c("0H", "48H")),
    # Parse replicate number safely: treat NC as 1, numeric codes as their number
    replicate_code_clean = dplyr::if_else(
      stringr::str_detect(replicate_code, "NC"),
      NA_character_,
      replicate_code
    ),
    replicate = readr::parse_number(replicate_code_clean),
    replicate = tidyr::replace_na(replicate, 1L),
    well_id = interaction(aliquot_id, carbohydrate, replicate, drop = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-replicate_code_clean) %>%
  dplyr::rename(SampleID = sample_id) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    SampleID, donor_id, aliquot_id, subject_id, customer_label,
    timepoint, carbohydrate, replicate, well_id, raw_seq_files
  )

tryCatch({
  healthy_lookup <- readr::read_tsv(
    file.path(
      "..", "microbiome_analysis", "zr24558.16S_250813.zymo",
      "1.Healthy.TimepointComparism..Bac16Sv34", "Sample_Information", "sample.metadata.csv"
    ),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  ) %>%
    janitor::clean_names() %>%
    separate(customer_label, into = c("aliquot_id", "tmp", "tp"), sep = "\\.", remove = FALSE) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      aliquot_id = stringr::str_to_upper(aliquot_id),
      donor_id = stringr::str_extract(aliquot_id, "^[0-9]+")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(donor_id) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(group = "Healthy")
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Error reading microbiome healthy lookup file: ", e$message)
})

micro_metadata <- micro_metadata %>%
  mutate(SampleID = paste0("S", customer_label)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    group = if_else(donor_id %in% healthy_lookup$donor_id, "Healthy", "Obese"),
    # Override MediaControl: group = NA, timepoint = "0H", carbohydrate = NA
    group = dplyr::if_else(
      stringr::str_detect(customer_label, regex("^MediaControl$", ignore_case = TRUE)),
      NA_character_,
      group
    ),
    timepoint = dplyr::if_else(
      stringr::str_detect(customer_label, regex("^MediaControl$", ignore_case = TRUE)),
      factor("0H", levels = levels(timepoint)),
      timepoint
    ),
    carbohydrate = dplyr::if_else(
      stringr::str_detect(customer_label, regex("^MediaControl$", ignore_case = TRUE)),
      factor(NA_character_, levels = levels(carbohydrate)),
      carbohydrate
    ),
    group = factor(group, levels = c("Healthy", "Obese")),
    donor_id = factor(donor_id),
    aliquot_id = factor(aliquot_id),
    subject_id = factor(subject_id),
    well_id = factor(well_id)
  )

micro_metadata <- micro_metadata %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(timepoint))

tryCatch({
  ps <- import_biom(
    file.path(
      "..", "microbiome_analysis", "zr24558.16S_250813.zymo",
      "00...AllSamples.Bac16Sv34", "DADA2_ASV_Distribution", "ASV_Table.biom"
    )
  )
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Error importing microbiome BIOM file: ", e$message)
})

colnames(tax_table(ps)) <- c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species")

sample_names(ps) <- paste0("S", sample_names(ps))

metadata_ps <- micro_metadata %>%
  dplyr::mutate(SampleID = as.character(SampleID)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(SampleID) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(SampleID = if (n() > 1) paste0(SampleID, "_", row_number()) else SampleID) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  column_to_rownames("SampleID")

sample_data(ps) <- sample_data(metadata_ps)

ps <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps) > 0, ps)
ps <- prune_samples(sample_sums(ps) > 0, ps)

# Primary clustering unit for person-level inference is donor_id (numeric person).
sample_data(ps)$donor_id <- as.character(sample_data(ps)$donor_id)
sample_data(ps)$aliquot_id <- as.character(sample_data(ps)$aliquot_id)
sample_data(ps)$SubjectID <- sample_data(ps)$donor_id
sample_data(ps)$Group <- sample_data(ps)$group
sample_data(ps)$Carbohydrate <- sample_data(ps)$carbohydrate
sample_data(ps)$Timepoint <- sample_data(ps)$timepoint

ps_rel <- phyloseq::transform_sample_counts(
  ps,
  function(x) {
    total <- sum(x)
    if (total > 0) x / total else x
  }
)

qpcr_data <- NULL

tryCatch({
  qpcr_data <- readr::read_csv(
    file.path(
      "..", "microbiome_analysis", "zr24558.16S_250813.zymo",
      "00...AllSamples.Bac16Sv34", "Sample_Information", "absolute.abundance.csv"
    ),
    show_col_types = FALSE
  ) %>%
    janitor::clean_names()
}, error = function(e) {
  warning("Unable to load qPCR absolute abundance data: ", e$message)
})

# Note:
```

# 1. Introduction

This integrated report brings together the short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) metabolomics and 16S rRNA gene microbiome analyses from the Lurie-Abbott carbohydrate obesity project. It re-runs the key components of each analysis within a single, reproducible R Markdown workflow and adds new integrative components relating taxa, SCFA concentrations, and responder phenotypes.

The goal is to maintain the rigor and depth of the original analyses while ensuring that metadata, filtering, and modeling decisions are harmonized across datasets.

# 2. Project Objectives

In this section, we summarize the main scientific and analytical objectives, building on the SCFA project objectives and extending them to explicitly include microbiome composition, diversity, and taxon–SCFA relationships.

# 3. Methods

This integrated analysis combines methods from both the SCFA metabolomics and 16S rRNA gene microbiome analyses. Below we describe the key methodological components employed throughout this report.

## 3.1 Study Design and Sample Processing

The study design includes two groups (Control/Healthy and Case/Obese) exposed to three carbohydrate conditions: no added carbohydrate (control), rapid digestible carbohydrate (RDC), and slow digestible carbohydrate (SDC). The analyzed SCFA and microbiome files contain 0H and 48H observations. Each numeric identifier is an independent person; A/B labels are sample-aliquot splits of that person's stool specimen; R1/R2 and S1/S2 denote culture-well replicates within each aliquot. Repeated observations are modeled with nested random intercepts for subject, aliquot, and well.

## 3.2 SCFA Quantification and Preprocessing

Short-chain fatty acids (butyrate, propionate, acetate, and others) were quantified using PFBBr derivatization and negative chemical-ionization GC-MS. The facility method documents authentic-standard calibration for acetate, propionate, butyrate, and succinate. The exported values are labeled micromolar (μM) in this workflow, but the unit and dilution mapping remain pending facility confirmation. The primary trajectory models use the exported concentration scale without log transformation.

## 3.3 Microbiome Sequencing, Processing, and Phyloseq Construction

16S rRNA gene sequencing was performed on fecal samples, and sequences were processed through standard quality control, denoising, and taxonomic assignment pipelines. The processed data were organized into a `phyloseq` object containing an OTU/ASV table, taxonomic classifications, sample metadata, and phylogenetic tree information. Relative abundances were calculated by normalizing counts to proportions within each sample. **qPCR-scaled abundances** were derived as genus relative abundance × total bacterial 16S qPCR load. These are estimated target equivalents, not genus-specific qPCR or cell counts. Facility confirmation of primers, efficiency, LOD/LOQ, and the `genome_copies_per_ul*` conversion footnote remains pending; claim-facing quantitative summaries should prefer `gene_copies_per_ul` when available (see `integrated/results/additional_analyses_2026-07-19/`).

## 3.4 Statistical Modeling Strategies

### 3.4.1 Mixed-Effects Models for SCFA Concentrations

Linear mixed-effects models were fitted to analyze SCFA concentrations as a function of group (Control vs Case), carbohydrate type, timepoint, and their interactions, with nested random intercepts for subject (numeric donor), A/B aliquot, and culture well. The well identifier is nested by construction within aliquot × carbohydrate and links the 0H and 48H observations from the same R1/R2, S1/S2, or no-added-carbohydrate culture. Type III ANOVA tables were generated to test main effects and interactions, with p-values adjusted using the Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) false discovery rate (FDR) procedure.

Interpersonal response heterogeneity was analyzed on one 0-to-48-hour change per donor × analyte × carbohydrate after averaging A/B aliquots and culture wells within donor and timepoint. Donor-aware repeated-measures models used `delta ~ group * carbohydrate + (1 | donor)`. Donor repeatability was summarized with the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) and a donor-resampling bootstrap confidence interval; rank consistency between RDC and SDC was summarized with Spearman correlation and a donor bootstrap interval. Obesity-group dispersion was described with donor-level standard deviations, obesity-to-healthy-weight SD ratios, bootstrap intervals, and Brown–Forsythe tests with BH correction across the six primary analyte × active-carbohydrate comparisons. Because responder status is defined from the same delta by a within-stratum median split, responder-versus-non-responder variance of that defining outcome was not tested.

The prespecified direct comparison of the butyrate response to SDC versus RDC was defined as the difference in 0-to-48-hour changes: (SDC 48H - SDC 0H) - (RDC 48H - RDC 0H). This difference-in-differences contrast was estimated from the same mixed-effects model using `emmeans`, marginalizing equally over obesity group. Two-sided inference is reported as the estimated difference in change in μM, a 95% confidence interval, and a Tukey-adjusted p-value controlling the family of three pairwise carbohydrate-change comparisons (RDC versus no added carbohydrate, SDC versus no added carbohydrate, and SDC versus RDC). This contrast, rather than the omnibus carbohydrate main effect or a time-averaged carbohydrate comparison, tests whether the butyrate increase is greater under SDC than RDC.

### 3.4.2 Obesity-Group Trajectory Contrasts and Equivalence

For each analyte and carbohydrate condition, the obesity-group estimand was `(Obesity 48H - Obesity 0H) - (Healthy-weight 48H - Healthy-weight 0H)`. The six primary contrasts were acetate, propionate, and butyrate under RDC and SDC. Model-based Wald 95% confidence intervals describe effect-estimate uncertainty; 90% confidence intervals are also reported because a formal two-one-sided-test (TOST) procedure would compare that interval with prespecified lower and upper equivalence bounds at α=0.05. Donor-level bootstrap intervals from 48H-minus-0H changes were used as a sensitivity analysis.

No external biological threshold, project-specific analyte CV/LOQ, or directly comparable ex vivo equivalence bound was available. Consequently, the margin specification remains unlocked, TOST p-values and equivalence verdicts are not calculated, and the smallest symmetric bound containing each observed 90% interval is reported only as a post hoc precision frontier. It must not be adopted as the equivalence margin. The full rationale is documented in `docs/scfa-obesity-equivalence-margin-spec.2026-07-19.md`.

### 3.4.3 Alpha Diversity Analysis

Within-sample microbial diversity was assessed using three metrics: Observed richness (number of unique taxa), Shannon diversity index (accounts for both richness and evenness), and Simpson diversity index (emphasizes dominant taxa). Metrics were averaged to one value per donor × carbohydrate × timepoint. Faceted Wilcoxon tables in this report are descriptive within-stratum comparisons. Claim-facing alpha inference uses donor-aware mixed models and group contrasts exported under `integrated/results/additional_analyses_2026-07-19/alpha_permanova/`.

### 3.4.4 Beta Diversity and Community Structure

Between-sample microbial community dissimilarity was quantified using Bray-Curtis distance on relative abundance data. Principal coordinates analysis (PCoA) was used to visualize community structure in reduced dimensions. Permutational multivariate analysis of variance (PERMANOVA) using `vegan::adonis2()` with 999 permutations was employed to test for significant differences in community composition between groups, carbohydrate conditions, and timepoints, with numeric donor ID as a stratification variable to account for repeated measures within person.

### 3.4.5 Differential Abundance Analysis

Two complementary methods were used to identify taxa that differ significantly between conditions:

**ANCOM-BC2**: Analysis of Compositions of Microbiomes with Bias Correction 2 was applied using the `ANCOMBC` package. This method accounts for compositionality and provides log-fold change estimates with bias correction, standard errors, and FDR-adjusted q-values. Models included group, carbohydrate, timepoint, and their interactions as fixed effects, with subject ID as a random effect where appropriate.

**MaAsLin2**: Microbiome Multivariable Association with Linear Models 2 was applied using the `Maaslin2` package. This method uses linear models with total sum scaling (TSS) normalization and log transformation. It provides coefficient estimates, standard errors, p-values, and FDR-adjusted q-values. Models included the same fixed and random effects as ANCOM-BC2 analyses.

Both methods were applied to relative abundance data, and results were filtered to retain associations with q < 0.1 (FDR-adjusted p-value threshold).

### 3.4.6 Taxon–SCFA Association Analysis

To identify microbial taxa associated with SCFA concentrations, ANCOM-BC2 and MaAsLin2 were applied with butyrate or propionate concentrations as continuous predictors, along with carbohydrate type and their interactions. These analyses were performed on relative abundance data and included subject ID as a random effect to account for repeated measures.

### 3.4.7 Correlation Analyses

Sample-level Spearman and ordinary linear models of relative *Fusicatenibacter* abundance versus SCFA at 48-hour SDC are retained in Section 7.4 only as descriptive diagnostics. They do **not** support claim-facing association statements because they treat nested wells as independent and do not implement exact well matching before aggregation. The claim-facing estimand is the donor-level SDC-attributable net change in log10 qPCR-scaled *Fusicatenibacter* versus Δbutyrate (N≈14–16 independent donors), reported under `integrated/results/additional_analyses_2026-07-19/focal_fusicatenibacter/`.

### 3.4.8 Responder vs Non-Responder Classification

Responder status was defined separately for butyrate and propionate from the donor-level change in SCFA concentration from baseline (0H) to 48H (delta = 48H - 0H). For each analyte and carbohydrate condition, donors were classified as "Responder" if their delta was greater than or equal to the within-stratum median and "Non-Responder" if below it. This is an exploratory, sample-dependent relative classification rather than a biological or clinical threshold. Classification sensitivity was assessed by applying the donor-level cutoff separately to the A and B aliquot changes. Variance of the defining delta was not compared between responder strata because such a comparison would condition on the outcome used to create the strata.

### 3.4.9 Responder Group Comparisons

Microbial composition differences between responder and non-responder groups were assessed using:
- Alpha diversity comparisons with Wilcoxon rank-sum tests
- Beta diversity comparisons using PERMANOVA
- Differential abundance analysis using ANCOM-BC2 and MaAsLin2 to identify taxa that differ between responder and non-responder groups

## 3.5 Integration Methods

SCFA and microbiome data were integrated by matching samples based on subject ID, timepoint, and carbohydrate condition. Metadata were harmonized to ensure consistent group labels (Control/Healthy, Case/Obese) and carbohydrate labels (No Added Carb, RDC, SDC) across datasets. The integrated metadata were added to the phyloseq object's sample data component to enable joint analyses.

## 3.6 Visualization and Reporting

All visualizations were created using `ggplot2` with a consistent color palette and theme derived from the SCFA analysis. Forest plots display effect sizes (log-fold changes) with 95% confidence intervals for ANCOM-BC2 results. Volcano plots show effect sizes versus significance for MaAsLin2 results. Alluvial diagrams illustrate compositional changes over time. Statistical test results are displayed directly on plots where appropriate (e.g., Wilcoxon p-values on boxplots, R² values on scatter plots). All p-values are reported with FDR adjustment where multiple comparisons were performed.


# 4. Summary Data

We begin with a concise overview of the sample counts by obesity status (Control vs Case) and carbohydrate condition across both SCFA and microbiome datasets.

```{r summary-data, echo=FALSE}
# Summary counts for SCFA (control/case) and microbiome (Healthy/Obese)

# SCFA: deduplicate to one row per biological sample (subject × timepoint × carbohydrate)
scfa_sample_overview <- scfa_sample_data_long_factored %>%
  dplyr::distinct(subject, group, carbohydrate_type, timepoint_hr) %>%
  mutate(
    group_label = factor(str_to_title(group), levels = c("Control", "Case")),
    carbohydrate = case_when(
      carbohydrate_type == "no_carbohydrate" ~ "No Added Carb",
      carbohydrate_type == "rapid_digestible" ~ "RDC",
      carbohydrate_type == "slow_digestible" ~ "SDC",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    carbohydrate = factor(carbohydrate, levels = c("No Added Carb", "RDC", "SDC"))
  )

scfa_summary_counts <- scfa_sample_overview %>%
  dplyr::count(group_label, carbohydrate, name = "n_samples") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(group_label, carbohydrate)

# Microbiome: sample counts by group and carbohydrate (all timepoints)
micro_summary_counts <- micro_metadata %>%
  dplyr::count(group, carbohydrate, timepoint, name = "n_samples") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(group, carbohydrate, timepoint)

scfa_table <- scfa_summary_counts %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    Group = group_label,
    Carbohydrate = carbohydrate,
    `N samples` = n_samples
  )

micro_table <- micro_summary_counts %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    Group = group,
    Carbohydrate = carbohydrate,
    Timepoint = timepoint,
    `N samples` = n_samples
  )

# Print SCFA table
if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  DT::datatable(
    scfa_table,
    caption = "SCFA samples by group and carbohydrate",
    options = list(pageLength = 10, dom = "tip"),
    rownames = FALSE
```

# 5. Metabolomics (SCFA)

## 5.1 Section Overview

This section reproduces and extends the SCFA analyses, focusing on:

- Carbohydrate type effects (combined and stratified by group)
- SCFA concentrations over time
- Advanced mixed-effects modeling for SCFA trajectories

We first quantify donor-level SCFA response magnitudes (48h – 0h), their repeatability across carbohydrates, and their dispersion by obesity group. We then visualize donor-averaged SCFA concentrations over time and fit linear mixed-effects models with nested subject, aliquot, and culture-well random effects to test fixed effects of group, carbohydrate type, time, and their interactions on absolute SCFA concentrations.

## 5.2 Donor-Level SCFA Response Variation

```{r scfa-carbohydrate-effects-prep, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# Prepare data for all plots (shared across chunks)
delta_data <- scfa_sample_data_long_factored %>%
  dplyr::filter(timepoint_hr %in% c("0", "48")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(
    subject, group, carbohydrate_type, timepoint_hr, analyte,
    group_label, carbohydrate_type_label
  ) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    concentration = mean(concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(subject, group, carbohydrate_type, analyte, group_label, carbohydrate_type_label),
    names_from = timepoint_hr,
    values_from = concentration,
    names_prefix = "time_"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(delta_48h_0h = time_48 - time_0) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(delta_48h_0h))

# Donor-aware repeated-measures models replace the one-way ANOVA that treated
# three carbohydrate records from the same donor as independent.
delta_mixed_results <- delta_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(analyte) %>%
  tidyr::nest() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    model = purrr::map(
      data,
      ~ lmerTest::lmer(
        delta_48h_0h ~ group * carbohydrate_type + (1 | subject),
        data = .x,
        REML = TRUE
      )
    ),
    anova_main = purrr::map(model, ~ as.data.frame(anova(.x)))
  )

delta_model_anova <- delta_mixed_results %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    anova_df = purrr::map(
      anova_main,
      ~ .x %>%
        tibble::rownames_to_column("effect") %>%
        tibble::as_tibble()
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(analyte, anova_df) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(anova_df) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    F_value = `F value`,
    p_value = `Pr(>F)`
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"),
    significance = dplyr::case_when(
      p_adj < 0.001 ~ "q<0.001",
      p_adj < 0.01 ~ "q<0.01",
      p_adj < 0.05 ~ "q<0.05",
      TRUE ~ "ns"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(p_adj)

extract_delta_icc <- function(model, donor_term = "subject") {
  variance_table <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(model))
  donor_variance <- variance_table$vcov[variance_table$grp == donor_term][1]
  residual_variance <- variance_table$vcov[variance_table$grp == "Residual"][1]
  c(
    donor_variance = donor_variance,
    residual_variance = residual_variance,
    icc = donor_variance / (donor_variance + residual_variance)
  )
}

bootstrap_delta_icc <- function(data, n_boot = 500) {
  donor_ids <- unique(as.character(data$subject))
  bootstrap_icc <- replicate(n_boot, {
    sampled_donors <- sample(donor_ids, length(donor_ids), replace = TRUE)
    bootstrap_data <- purrr::map2_dfr(
      sampled_donors,
      seq_along(sampled_donors),
      function(donor, bootstrap_id) {
        data %>%
          dplyr::filter(as.character(subject) == donor) %>%
          dplyr::mutate(subject_boot = factor(bootstrap_id))
      }
    )
    if (dplyr::n_distinct(bootstrap_data$group) < 2) {
      return(NA_real_)
    }
    bootstrap_model <- try(
      suppressWarnings(
        lme4::lmer(
          delta_48h_0h ~ group * carbohydrate_type + (1 | subject_boot),
          data = bootstrap_data,
          REML = TRUE
        )
      ),
      silent = TRUE
    )
    if (inherits(bootstrap_model, "try-error")) {
      return(NA_real_)
    }
    extract_delta_icc(bootstrap_model, donor_term = "subject_boot")[["icc"]]
  })
  stats::quantile(
    bootstrap_icc[is.finite(bootstrap_icc)],
    probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
    na.rm = TRUE,
    names = FALSE
  )
}

set.seed(2720)
delta_repeatability_summary <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
  delta_mixed_results %>% dplyr::select(analyte, data, model),
  function(analyte, data, model) {
    variance_estimates <- extract_delta_icc(model)
    icc_interval <- bootstrap_delta_icc(data)
    tibble::tibble(
      analyte = analyte,
      donor_variance = variance_estimates[["donor_variance"]],
      residual_variance = variance_estimates[["residual_variance"]],
      icc = variance_estimates[["icc"]],
      icc_ci_lower = icc_interval[1],
      icc_ci_upper = icc_interval[2]
    )
  }
)

bootstrap_spearman <- function(data, n_boot = 2000) {
  bootstrap_rho <- replicate(n_boot, {
    sampled_rows <- sample(seq_len(nrow(data)), nrow(data), replace = TRUE)
    sampled_data <- data[sampled_rows, , drop = FALSE]
    if (
      dplyr::n_distinct(sampled_data$rapid_digestible) < 2 ||
        dplyr::n_distinct(sampled_data$slow_digestible) < 2
    ) {
      return(NA_real_)
    }
    stats::cor(
      sampled_data$rapid_digestible,
      sampled_data$slow_digestible,
      method = "spearman"
    )
  })
  stats::quantile(
    bootstrap_rho[is.finite(bootstrap_rho)],
    probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
    na.rm = TRUE,
    names = FALSE
  )
}

set.seed(2720)
rdc_sdc_rank_summary <- delta_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    carbohydrate_type %in% c("rapid_digestible", "slow_digestible")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(subject, analyte, carbohydrate_type, delta_48h_0h) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = carbohydrate_type,
    values_from = delta_48h_0h
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(analyte) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(
    ~ {
      rank_test <- suppressWarnings(
        stats::cor.test(
          .x$rapid_digestible,
          .x$slow_digestible,
          method = "spearman",
          exact = FALSE
        )
      )
      rank_interval <- bootstrap_spearman(.x)
      tibble::tibble(
        n_donors = nrow(.x),
        spearman_rho = unname(rank_test$estimate),
        p_value = rank_test$p.value,
        rho_ci_lower = rank_interval[1],
        rho_ci_upper = rank_interval[2]
      )
    }
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

primary_active_delta <- delta_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    analyte %in% c("acetate", "propionate", "butyrate"),
    carbohydrate_type %in% c("rapid_digestible", "slow_digestible")
  )

bootstrap_sd_ratio <- function(data, n_boot = 5000) {
  healthy <- data$delta_48h_0h[data$group == "control"]
  obesity <- data$delta_48h_0h[data$group == "case"]
  bootstrap_ratios <- replicate(n_boot, {
    healthy_sd <- stats::sd(sample(healthy, length(healthy), replace = TRUE))
    obesity_sd <- stats::sd(sample(obesity, length(obesity), replace = TRUE))
    if (!is.finite(healthy_sd) || healthy_sd <= 0) {
      return(NA_real_)
    }
    obesity_sd / healthy_sd
  })
  stats::quantile(
    bootstrap_ratios[is.finite(bootstrap_ratios)],
    probs = c(0.025, 0.975),
    na.rm = TRUE,
    names = FALSE
  )
}

set.seed(2720)
delta_group_dispersion_summary <- primary_active_delta %>%
  dplyr::group_by(analyte, carbohydrate_type) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(
    ~ {
      group_summary <- .x %>%
        dplyr::group_by(group) %>%
        dplyr::summarise(
          n = dplyr::n(),
          mean_delta = mean(delta_48h_0h),
          sd_delta = stats::sd(delta_48h_0h),
          median_delta = stats::median(delta_48h_0h),
          iqr_delta = stats::IQR(delta_48h_0h),
          .groups = "drop"
        ) %>%
        tidyr::pivot_wider(
          names_from = group,
          values_from = c(n, mean_delta, sd_delta, median_delta, iqr_delta),
          names_sep = "_"
        )

      brown_forsythe_data <- .x %>%
        dplyr::group_by(group) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(
          absolute_median_deviation = abs(
            delta_48h_0h - stats::median(delta_48h_0h)
          )
        ) %>%
        dplyr::ungroup()
      brown_forsythe_anova <- anova(
        stats::lm(absolute_median_deviation ~ group, data = brown_forsythe_data)
      )
      ratio_interval <- bootstrap_sd_ratio(.x)

      group_summary %>%
        dplyr::mutate(
          sd_ratio_obesity_healthy = sd_delta_case / sd_delta_control,
          sd_ratio_ci_lower = ratio_interval[1],
          sd_ratio_ci_upper = ratio_interval[2],
          brown_forsythe_F = brown_forsythe_anova$`F value`[1],
          brown_forsythe_p = brown_forsythe_anova$`Pr(>F)`[1]
        )
    }
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    brown_forsythe_q = p.adjust(brown_forsythe_p, method = "BH")
  )
```

## 5.4 Advanced Statistical Modeling: Mixed-Effects Models

```{r scfa-mixed-effects, echo=FALSE}
# Mixed-effects models for absolute SCFA concentrations
mixed_effects_results <- scfa_sample_data_long_factored %>%
  dplyr::group_by(analyte) %>%
  tidyr::nest() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Use lmerTest::lmer so that anova() returns F-tests with p-values
    model = purrr::map(
      data,
      ~ lmerTest::lmer(
        concentration ~ group * carbohydrate_type * timepoint_hr +
          (1 | subject) + (1 | aliquot_id) + (1 | well_id),
        data = .x
      )
    ),
    anova_main = purrr::map(model, ~ anova(.x)),
    model_summary = purrr::map(model, ~ summary(.x))
  )

main_anova_summary <- mixed_effects_results %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    anova_df = purrr::map(
      anova_main,
      ~ as.data.frame(.x) %>%
        tibble::rownames_to_column("effect")
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(analyte, anova_df) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(anova_df) %>%
  dplyr::filter(effect != "Residual") %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    F_value = `F value`,
    pr_f = `Pr(>F)`
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    p_adj = p.adjust(pr_f, method = "BH"),
    significance = dplyr::case_when(
      p_adj < 0.001 ~ "p<0.001",
      p_adj < 0.01 ~ "p<0.01",
      p_adj < 0.05 ~ "p<0.05",
      TRUE ~ "ns"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(p_adj)

if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  DT::datatable(
    main_anova_summary %>%
      dplyr::select(analyte, effect, F_value, pr_f, p_adj, significance),
    caption = "Mixed-Effects Models for SCFA Concentrations: ANOVA Table",
    options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE),
    rownames = FALSE
  ) %>%
    DT::formatRound(columns = c("F_value", "pr_f", "p_adj"), digits = 4)
} else {
  knitr::kable(
    main_anova_summary %>%
      dplyr::select(analyte, effect, F_value, pr_f, p_adj, significance),
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Mixed-Effects Models for SCFA Concentrations: ANOVA Table"
  )
}
```

### 5.4.1 Variance Decomposition of SCFA Concentrations

```{r scfa-variance-components, echo=FALSE, fig.width=12, fig.height=6, cache=FALSE, dependson="scfa-mixed-effects"}
variance_component_summary <- mixed_effects_results %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    analyte,
    variance_components = purrr::map(
      model,
      ~ as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(.x)) %>%
        dplyr::transmute(
          component = dplyr::case_when(
            grp == "subject" ~ "Donor",
            grp == "aliquot_id" ~ "Aliquot",
            grp == "well_id" ~ "Culture well",
            grp == "Residual" ~ "Residual",
            TRUE ~ as.character(grp)
          ),
          variance = vcov
        )
    )
  ) %>%
  tidyr::unnest(variance_components) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(analyte) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    total_random_residual_variance = sum(variance),
    variance_proportion = variance / total_random_residual_variance
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    component = factor(
      component,
      levels = c("Donor", "Aliquot", "Culture well", "Residual")
    )
  )

    variance_component_table,
    digits = 3,
    caption = "Variance components from nested SCFA concentration models"
  )
}
```

### 5.4.2 Adjusted SDC-versus-RDC Butyrate Response Contrast

```{r butyrate-sdc-rdc-contrast, echo=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
# The response estimand is the difference in 0-to-48-hour change:
# (SDC 48H - SDC 0H) - (RDC 48H - RDC 0H).
butyrate_model <- mixed_effects_results %>%
  dplyr::filter(analyte == "butyrate") %>%
  dplyr::pull(model) %>%
  purrr::pluck(1)

# Estimate the 48H - 0H change separately for each carbohydrate condition.
butyrate_time_emm <- emmeans::emmeans(
  butyrate_model,
  ~ timepoint_hr | carbohydrate_type,
  weights = "equal"
)

butyrate_changes <- emmeans::contrast(
  butyrate_time_emm,
  method = "revpairwise",
  by = "carbohydrate_type"
)

# Compare the three carbohydrate-specific changes, with Tukey adjustment.
butyrate_change_results <- pairs(
  butyrate_changes,
  by = NULL,
  reverse = TRUE,
  adjust = "tukey"
) %>%
  summary(infer = c(TRUE, TRUE), adjust = "tukey") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble::as_tibble()

butyrate_sdc_rdc <- butyrate_change_results %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    stringr::str_detect(
      contrast,
      "slow_digestible.*rapid_digestible"
    )
  )

if (nrow(butyrate_sdc_rdc) != 1) {
  stop("Unable to identify a unique SDC-versus-RDC butyrate change contrast.")
}

butyrate_delta_summary <- delta_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    analyte == "butyrate",
    carbohydrate_type %in% c("rapid_digestible", "slow_digestible")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(carbohydrate_type) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_delta = mean(delta_48h_0h, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_delta = sd(delta_48h_0h, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_subject_ids = dplyr::n_distinct(subject),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

butyrate_rdc_mean_delta <- butyrate_delta_summary %>%
  dplyr::filter(carbohydrate_type == "rapid_digestible") %>%
  dplyr::pull(mean_delta)

butyrate_sdc_mean_delta <- butyrate_delta_summary %>%
  dplyr::filter(carbohydrate_type == "slow_digestible") %>%
  dplyr::pull(mean_delta)

if (knitr::is_html_output()) {
  DT::datatable(
    butyrate_change_results %>%
      dplyr::select(
        contrast, estimate, SE, df, lower.CL, upper.CL, t.ratio, p.value
      ),
    caption = paste(
      "Adjusted pairwise comparisons of 0-to-48-hour butyrate change",
      "(Tukey-adjusted within the three carbohydrate comparisons)"
    ),
    options = list(pageLength = 10, dom = "tip", scrollX = TRUE),
    rownames = FALSE
  ) %>%
    DT::formatRound(
      columns = c("estimate", "SE", "df", "lower.CL", "upper.CL", "t.ratio", "p.value"),
      digits = 3
    )
} else {
  knitr::kable(
    butyrate_change_results %>%
      dplyr::select(
        contrast, estimate, SE, df, lower.CL, upper.CL, t.ratio, p.value
      ),
    digits = 3,
    caption = paste(
      "Adjusted pairwise comparisons of 0-to-48-hour butyrate change",
      "(Tukey-adjusted within the three carbohydrate comparisons)"
    )
  )
}
```

The mean 0-to-48-hour butyrate change was `r sprintf("%.2f", butyrate_sdc_mean_delta)` μM under SDC and `r sprintf("%.2f", butyrate_rdc_mean_delta)` μM under RDC. The model-adjusted SDC-versus-RDC difference in change was `r sprintf("%.2f", butyrate_sdc_rdc$estimate)` μM (95% CI, `r sprintf("%.2f", butyrate_sdc_rdc$lower.CL)` to `r sprintf("%.2f", butyrate_sdc_rdc$upper.CL)`; Tukey-adjusted p = `r format.pval(butyrate_sdc_rdc$p.value, digits = 3, eps = 0.001)`). Thus, the butyrate increase was numerically greater under SDC, but the current analysis does not demonstrate that SDC produces a greater butyrate response than RDC.

This estimate uses the corrected biological-unit hierarchy: numeric subject (independent person), A/B sample aliquots nested within subject, and R1/R2 or S1/S2 culture wells nested within aliquot. The concentration unit remains provisional pending facility confirmation.

Across the six primary contrasts, the estimated obesity-minus-healthy-weight differences in 0-to-48-hour change were −0.09 μM (95% CI −5.17 to 5.00) for acetate under RDC, 3.43 μM (−1.66 to 8.51) for acetate under SDC, 0.74 μM (−0.70 to 2.18) for propionate under RDC, 0.38 μM (−1.06 to 1.82) for propionate under SDC, −0.76 μM (−2.96 to 1.44) for butyrate under RDC, and −1.19 μM (−3.39 to 1.02) for butyrate under SDC. None differed significantly from zero. Donor-level bootstrap intervals, resampling the 16 independent subjects, gave the same qualitative conclusion. Because no externally justified equivalence margin is locked, these intervals do not establish equivalence or preserved fermentation capacity.

Residual diagnostics indicated non-normality for all analytes and heteroscedasticity for propionate and butyrate; the donor-level bootstrap intervals are therefore retained as a sensitivity analysis. Several aliquot- or well-level variance components were near the boundary; the subject-level random intercept remained the primary clustering term.

## 5.6 Summary of SCFA Results

The SCFA metabolomics analysis reveals several key findings regarding short-chain fatty acid production in response to carbohydrate challenge in adolescents with and without obesity:

**1. Dominant Effect of Carbohydrate Type and Time**

The primary drivers of SCFA production in this ex vivo model were the type of carbohydrate supplied and the incubation time. This was supported by:
- Donor-aware mixed models of 0-to-48-hour change (delta ~ group × carbohydrate + (1 | donor); Section 5.2)
- Clear temporal increases in SCFA concentrations, with distinct trajectories by carbohydrate condition (Section 5.3)
- Significant carbohydrate, timepoint, and selected carbohydrate-by-timepoint effects in the nested mixed-effects models (Section 5.4)

Donor-aware carbohydrate-change contrasts for acetate, propionate, and butyrate are also exported under `results/additional_analyses_2026-07-19/scfa_contrasts/`. The omnibus or main effects do not establish every pairwise carbohydrate difference. For butyrate, the adjusted 0-to-48-hour change was greater for SDC than no added carbohydrate, whereas the RDC-versus-no-added-carbohydrate and SDC-versus-RDC contrasts were not significant after Tukey adjustment (Section 5.4.2).

**2. Obesity-Group Contrasts Were Nonsignificant but Not Equivalent**

No primary obesity-group difference-in-change contrast differed significantly from zero. The 95% confidence intervals nevertheless included differences that could be scientifically important, especially for acetate. Because no externally justified analyte-specific margin is available, this analysis cannot establish equivalence, non-inferiority, preserved capacity, or an unaffected fermentation response.

**3. Carbohydrate-Specific Response Patterns**

The analyses revealed distinct response patterns for different carbohydrate types:
- Both RDC and SDC showed descriptive increases in SCFA production, but adjusted condition-specific support varied by analyte and contrast
- The magnitude and timing of responses varied by carbohydrate type, as evidenced by significant carbohydrate × timepoint interactions in the mixed-effects models
- These differences highlight the importance of carbohydrate structure and digestibility in shaping microbial metabolic output

**4. Donor-Level Response Heterogeneity and Repeatability**

After averaging replicate measurements within each donor, 0-to-48-hour SCFA changes varied among the 16 independent donors. Donor rankings were reproducible between RDC and SDC: `r paste(sprintf("%s rho = %.2f (95%% bootstrap CI %.2f to %.2f)", stringr::str_to_title(rdc_sdc_rank_summary$analyte[rdc_sdc_rank_summary$analyte %in% c("acetate", "propionate", "butyrate")]), rdc_sdc_rank_summary$spearman_rho[rdc_sdc_rank_summary$analyte %in% c("acetate", "propionate", "butyrate")], rdc_sdc_rank_summary$rho_ci_lower[rdc_sdc_rank_summary$analyte %in% c("acetate", "propionate", "butyrate")], rdc_sdc_rank_summary$rho_ci_upper[rdc_sdc_rank_summary$analyte %in% c("acetate", "propionate", "butyrate")]), collapse = "; ")`. In donor-aware delta models spanning all three carbohydrate conditions, the corresponding ICCs were `r paste(sprintf("%s %.2f (95%% bootstrap CI %.2f to %.2f)", stringr::str_to_title(delta_repeatability_summary$analyte[delta_repeatability_summary$analyte %in% c("acetate", "propionate", "butyrate")]), delta_repeatability_summary$icc[delta_repeatability_summary$analyte %in% c("acetate", "propionate", "butyrate")], delta_repeatability_summary$icc_ci_lower[delta_repeatability_summary$analyte %in% c("acetate", "propionate", "butyrate")], delta_repeatability_summary$icc_ci_upper[delta_repeatability_summary$analyte %in% c("acetate", "propionate", "butyrate")]), collapse = "; ")`.

These results support a general donor tendency toward higher or lower SCFA response across carbohydrate conditions; they do not demonstrate that each donor has a unique carbohydrate-specific response. A donor × carbohydrate variance component or independent validation would be needed for that stronger claim.

Across acetate, propionate, and butyrate under RDC and SDC, obesity-to-healthy-weight SD ratios ranged from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(delta_group_dispersion_summary$sd_ratio_obesity_healthy))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(delta_group_dispersion_summary$sd_ratio_obesity_healthy))`; no Brown–Forsythe comparison was significant after BH correction (minimum q = `r format.pval(min(delta_group_dispersion_summary$brown_forsythe_q), digits = 3)`). With eight donors per group, this is evidence of no detected dispersion difference rather than evidence that group variances are equivalent.

**5. Statistical Model Insights**

The linear mixed-effects models (Section 5.4) provide formal statistical confirmation of these patterns, accounting for repeated measures within subjects. Key model findings include:
- Significant main effects of carbohydrate type and timepoint across multiple SCFAs
- Significant interactions between carbohydrate type and timepoint, indicating that the temporal response depends on the carbohydrate substrate
- Nonsignificant group contrasts whose confidence intervals do not support an equivalence claim
- Variance components and donor-level ICCs quantify persistent donor differences, while bootstrap intervals convey their uncertainty

These findings set the stage for the integrated analyses in Section 7, where we examine how microbial composition relates to SCFA production patterns and identify specific taxa associated with SCFA concentrations and responder phenotypes.

# 6. Microbiome

## 6.1 Section Overview

This section reproduces key microbiome results, including alpha and beta diversity, community composition, and differential abundance, using the harmonized metadata and styling. We focus first on within-sample diversity (alpha diversity) to summarize richness and evenness patterns across groups, carbohydrate conditions, and timepoints, then move to between-sample diversity (beta diversity) and taxon-level changes.

## 6.2 Alpha Diversity

```{r alpha-diversity, echo=FALSE, fig.width=18, fig.height=8, cache=FALSE}
# Alpha diversity metrics: Observed, Shannon, Simpson at 0H and 48H

alpha_metrics <- estimate_richness(ps, measures = c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson")) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("SampleID")

alpha_long <- alpha_metrics %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = -SampleID,
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(micro_metadata, by = "SampleID") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    metric = factor(metric, levels = c("Shannon", "Observed", "Simpson"))
  )

alpha_long_0_48 <- alpha_long %>%
  dplyr::filter(timepoint %in% c("0H", "48H"))

# Person-level grain for claim-facing alpha tests: mean across A/B wells within donor cell.
alpha_donor_0_48 <- alpha_long_0_48 %>%
  dplyr::group_by(donor_id, group, carbohydrate, timepoint, metric) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Alpha diversity boxplots by group, carbohydrate, and timepoint
# with per-facet Healthy vs Obese Wilcoxon p-values
alpha_plot <- alpha_donor_0_48 %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = carbohydrate, y = value, fill = group)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.8, outlier.shape = NA, position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  geom_jitter(
    aes(color = group),
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 1.2,
    position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.8)
  ) +
  ggpubr::stat_compare_means(
    aes(group = group),
    method = "wilcox.test",
    label = "p.format",
    label.y = Inf,
    vjust = 1.5
  ) +
  facet_grid(metric ~ timepoint, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_scfa() +
  scale_color_scfa() +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = "Alpha Diversity by Group, Carbohydrate, and Timepoint",
    subtitle = "Each point is one donor (mean across A/B culture wells within the cell)",
    x = "Carbohydrate",
    y = "Diversity metric"
  ) +
  theme_scfa() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Summaries at 48H for combined groups modeling
alpha_48h <- alpha_donor_0_48 %>%
  dplyr::filter(timepoint == "48H")

alpha_48h_summary <- alpha_48h %>%
  dplyr::group_by(metric, group, carbohydrate) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    n = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Wilcoxon tests: Healthy vs Obese within carbohydrate × timepoint for each alpha metric
# (donor-aggregated values; one observation per donor × carbohydrate × timepoint)
alpha_wilcox_group <- tryCatch({
  alpha_donor_0_48 %>%
    dplyr::group_by(metric, carbohydrate, timepoint) %>%
    dplyr::filter(dplyr::n_distinct(group) == 2) %>%  # Only test if both groups present
    rstatix::wilcox_test(value ~ group, p.adjust.method = "BH") %>%
    rstatix::add_significance() %>%
    dplyr::ungroup()
}, error = function(e) {
  cat("Error calculating alpha_wilcox_group:", e$message, "\n")
  tibble::tibble()
})

# Check available columns and select appropriate ones
if (nrow(alpha_wilcox_group) > 0) {
  # Check what columns exist (p.adj vs p_adjust)
  p_adj_col <- intersect(c("p.adj", "p_adjust", "adj.p.value"), names(alpha_wilcox_group))
  p_adj_col <- if (length(p_adj_col) > 0) p_adj_col[1] else NULL
  
  p_signif_col <- intersect(c("p.adj.signif", "p_adjust_signif", "signif"), names(alpha_wilcox_group))
  p_signif_col <- if (length(p_signif_col) > 0) p_signif_col[1] else NULL
  
  # Create adjusted p-value if it doesn't exist
  if (is.null(p_adj_col) && "p" %in% names(alpha_wilcox_group)) {
    alpha_wilcox_group$p_adj <- p.adjust(alpha_wilcox_group$p, method = "BH")
  } else if (!is.null(p_adj_col)) {
    alpha_wilcox_group$p_adj <- alpha_wilcox_group[[p_adj_col]]
  } else {
    alpha_wilcox_group$p_adj <- NA_real_
  }
  
  # Create significance column if it doesn't exist
  if (is.null(p_signif_col)) {
    alpha_wilcox_group$p_adj_signif <- dplyr::case_when(
      alpha_wilcox_group$p_adj < 0.001 ~ "***",
      alpha_wilcox_group$p_adj < 0.01 ~ "**",
      alpha_wilcox_group$p_adj < 0.05 ~ "*",
      alpha_wilcox_group$p_adj < 0.1 ~ ".",
      TRUE ~ "ns"
    )
  } else {
    alpha_wilcox_group$p_adj_signif <- alpha_wilcox_group[[p_signif_col]]
  }
  
  alpha_wilcox_group <- alpha_wilcox_group %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      comparison = paste0(group1, " vs ", group2),
      metric_carb_time = paste(metric, carbohydrate, timepoint, sep = " | ")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(metric, carbohydrate, timepoint, comparison, p, p_adj, p_adj_signif)
} else {
  alpha_wilcox_group <- tibble::tibble(
    metric = character(0),
    carbohydrate = character(0),
    timepoint = character(0),
    comparison = character(0),
    p = numeric(0),
    p_adj = numeric(0),
    p_adj_signif = character(0)
  )
}

# Wilcoxon tests: Carbohydrate comparisons within group × timepoint for each alpha metric

  # Create significance column if it doesn't exist
```

## 6.3 Beta Diversity

```{r beta-diversity, echo=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=10, cache=FALSE}
# Beta diversity and community structure using Bray-Curtis distance

# Helper: PCoA data frame
make_pcoa_df <- function(ps_obj, distance_method) {
  ord <- ordinate(ps_obj, method = "PCoA", distance = distance_method)
  vecs <- as_tibble(ord$vectors[, 1:2], rownames = "SampleID")
  colnames(vecs)[2:3] <- c("PC1", "PC2")
  vecs <- vecs %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      axis1_var = ord$values$Relative_eig[1],
      axis2_var = ord$values$Relative_eig[2]
    ) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(
      as_tibble(micro_metadata, .name_repair = "minimal"),
      by = "SampleID"
    )
  vecs
}

# Bray-Curtis PCoA across all samples
pcoa_bray <- make_pcoa_df(ps_rel, "bray")

# PERMANOVA: group × carbohydrate + timepoint with donor-level strata
dist_bray <- phyloseq::distance(ps_rel, method = "bray")
df_beta <- as(sample_data(ps_rel), "data.frame")

permanova_bray <- vegan::adonis2(
  dist_bray ~ group * carbohydrate + timepoint,
  data = df_beta,
  permutations = 999,
  strata = df_beta$donor_id
)

permanova_bray_tbl <- as.data.frame(permanova_bray) %>%
  rownames_to_column("term") %>%
  janitor::clean_names()

# Try to standardize column names for downstream use
permanova_bray_p_col <- intersect(
  c("pr_greater_f_", "pr_greater_f", "pr_f", "p_value"),
  names(permanova_bray_tbl)
)
permanova_bray_p_col <- if (length(permanova_bray_p_col) > 0) permanova_bray_p_col[1] else NULL

permanova_bray_f_col <- intersect(
  c("f", "f_model", "pseudo_f"),
  names(permanova_bray_tbl)
)
permanova_bray_f_col <- if (length(permanova_bray_f_col) > 0) permanova_bray_f_col[1] else NULL

permanova_bray_r2_col <- intersect(
  c("r2", "r_squared", "r2_adj"),
  names(permanova_bray_tbl)
)
permanova_bray_r2_col <- if (length(permanova_bray_r2_col) > 0) permanova_bray_r2_col[1] else NULL

# Create standardized columns if they don't exist
if (!is.null(permanova_bray_f_col)) {
  permanova_bray_tbl$f <- permanova_bray_tbl[[permanova_bray_f_col]]
} else if ("f" %in% names(permanova_bray_tbl)) {
  permanova_bray_tbl$f <- permanova_bray_tbl$f
} else {
  permanova_bray_tbl$f <- NA_real_
}

if (!is.null(permanova_bray_r2_col)) {
  permanova_bray_tbl$r2 <- permanova_bray_tbl[[permanova_bray_r2_col]]
} else if ("r2" %in% names(permanova_bray_tbl)) {
  permanova_bray_tbl$r2 <- permanova_bray_tbl$r2
} else {
  permanova_bray_tbl$r2 <- NA_real_
}

if (!is.null(permanova_bray_p_col)) {
  permanova_bray_tbl$p_value <- permanova_bray_tbl[[permanova_bray_p_col]]
} else if ("p_value" %in% names(permanova_bray_tbl)) {
  permanova_bray_tbl$p_value <- permanova_bray_tbl$p_value
} else {
  permanova_bray_tbl$p_value <- NA_real_
}

# PCoA plot with PERMANOVA annotation (R² and p for group:carbohydrate)
permanova_gc <- permanova_bray_tbl %>%
  dplyr::filter(term == "group:carbohydrate")

annotation_text <- NULL
if (nrow(permanova_gc) > 0 && !is.na(permanova_gc$r2[1]) && !is.na(permanova_gc$p_value[1])) {
  annotation_text <- as.character(glue::glue(
    "R² = {round(permanova_gc$r2[1], 3)}, p = {signif(permanova_gc$p_value[1], 3)}"
  ))
}

beta_pcoa_plot <- {
  p <- pcoa_bray %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = carbohydrate, shape = group)) +
    geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.85) +
    stat_ellipse(
      aes(group = interaction(carbohydrate, timepoint), color = carbohydrate),
      linewidth = 0.4,
      linetype = "dashed",
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~timepoint) +
    scale_color_scfa() +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17)) +
    labs(
      x = paste0("PC1 (", scales::percent(round(pcoa_bray$axis1_var[1], 3)), ")"),
      y = paste0("PC2 (", scales::percent(round(pcoa_bray$axis2_var[1], 3)), ")"),
      title = "PCoA – Bray-Curtis distance"
    ) +
    theme_scfa()

  if (!is.null(annotation_text)) {
    p <- p +
      annotate(
        "label",
        x = -Inf,
        y = Inf,
        hjust = -0.05,
        vjust = 1.1,
        label = annotation_text,
        size = 3,
        fontface = "bold",
        fill = "white",
        alpha = 0.8
      )
  }

  p
}

# 48H-only Bray-Curtis PCoA and PERMANOVA
```

## 6.4 Community Composition


### 6.4.1 Genus-Level Aggregation and Overview

```{r genus-aggregation, echo=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=10, cache=FALSE}
# Create genus-level aggregation using tax_glom
ps_genus <- tax_glom(ps, taxrank = "Genus", NArm = FALSE)
ps_genus <- prune_taxa(taxa_sums(ps_genus) > 0, ps_genus)

# Keep only top 20 most abundant genera for visualization
genus_abundance <- sort(taxa_sums(ps_genus), decreasing = TRUE)
top_genera <- names(genus_abundance)[1:min(20, length(genus_abundance))]
ps_genus <- prune_taxa(top_genera, ps_genus)

# Genus-level bar plots by group, carbohydrate, and timepoint
ps_genus_rel <- transform_sample_counts(ps_genus, function(x) x / sum(x))

genus_barplot_all <- psmelt(ps_genus_rel) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = carbohydrate, y = Abundance, fill = Genus)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  facet_grid(group ~ timepoint) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = scico::scico(21, palette = "batlow")) +
  labs(
    x = "Carbohydrate",
    y = "Relative abundance",
    title = "Genus-level composition by group, carbohydrate, and timepoint",
    fill = "Genus"
  ) +
  theme_scfa() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Genus-level bar plot at 48H only
ps_48h_genus <- phyloseq::subset_samples(ps_genus, timepoint == "48H")

genus_barplot_48h <- psmelt(transform_sample_counts(ps_48h_genus, function(x) x / sum(x))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = carbohydrate, y = Abundance, fill = Genus)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  facet_wrap(~ group) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = scico::scico(21, palette = "batlow")) +
  labs(
    x = "Carbohydrate",
    y = "Relative abundance",
    title = "Genus-level composition at 48H",
    fill = "Genus"
  ) +
  theme_scfa() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Print plots
print(genus_barplot_all)
print(genus_barplot_48h)
```

### 6.4.2 Genus Composition Changes from 0H to 48H by Carbohydrate Type

```{r genus-alluvial, echo=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=10, cache=FALSE}
# Prepare data for alluvial diagrams showing flow from 0H to 48H
ps_genus_rel <- transform_sample_counts(ps_genus, function(x) x / sum(x))

# Extract data
otu_mat <- as.matrix(otu_table(ps_genus_rel))
if (!taxa_are_rows(ps_genus_rel)) {
  otu_mat <- t(otu_mat)
}

tax_df <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps_genus_rel))
meta_df <- data.frame(sample_data(ps_genus_rel)) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("SampleID")

# Create long format data
alluvial_data_raw <- otu_mat %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("ASV") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-ASV, names_to = "SampleID", values_to = "Abundance") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    tax_df %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("ASV") %>% dplyr::select(ASV, Genus),
    by = "ASV"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    meta_df %>% dplyr::select(SampleID, timepoint, carbohydrate),
    by = "SampleID"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(timepoint %in% c("0H", "48H"))

# Remove NA values and filter to only valid combinations
alluvial_data_raw_clean <- alluvial_data_raw %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(Abundance),
    !is.na(Genus),
    !is.na(timepoint),
    !is.na(carbohydrate)
  )

# Group by Genus, timepoint, carbohydrate to get mean abundance
# Use na.rm = TRUE to handle any remaining edge cases
alluvial_data_grouped <- alluvial_data_raw_clean %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Genus, timepoint, carbohydrate) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(mean_abundance = mean(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Get top 12 genera for visualization (use max abundance across all timepoints/carbs)
# But don't filter the data yet - we'll use all data and then aggregate
top_genera_by_abundance <- alluvial_data_grouped %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Genus) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(max_abund = max(mean_abundance), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(max_abund)) %>%
  head(12) %>%
  dplyr::pull(Genus)

# Define genera that are important from DA analysis and should be included
# Check with single underscore "g_", double underscore "g__", and without prefix
# since taxonomy formats may vary (tax_table uses "g__" format)
da_important_genera <- c(
  "g_Fusicatenibacter",
  "g__Fusicatenibacter",
  "Fusicatenibacter",
  "g_Fusicatenibacters",
  "g__Fusicatenibacters",
  "Fusicatenibacters",
  "g_Hungatella",
  "g__Hungatella",
  "Hungatella",
  "g_Eggerthella",
  "g__Eggerthella",
  "Eggerthella",
  "g_Peptoniphilus",
  "g__Peptoniphilus",
  "Peptoniphilus"
)

# Check which of these genera exist in the data
# IMPORTANT: Get available_genera from the original tax_table, not from grouped data
# This ensures we find all genera in the taxonomy, even if they have zero/low abundance
available_genera_from_tax <- unique(tax_df$Genus)
available_genera_grouped <- unique(alluvial_data_grouped$Genus)

# Check exact matches first
da_genera_in_data <- da_important_genera[da_important_genera %in% available_genera_from_tax]

# Also check for variations in the full taxonomy (e.g., "g__Fusicatenibacter sp." might be stored differently)
# This will catch any genus containing these names, regardless of prefix or suffix
da_genera_variations <- available_genera_from_tax[
  stringr::str_detect(available_genera_from_tax, regex("Fusicatenibacter|Hungatella|Eggerthella|Peptoniphilus", ignore_case = TRUE))
]

# Combine exact matches and variations
da_genera_found <- unique(c(da_genera_in_data, da_genera_variations))

# Combine top 12 by abundance with DA-important genera
# Remove duplicates and keep up to 16 genera total
top_genera_alluvial <- unique(c(top_genera_by_abundance, da_genera_found))
if (length(top_genera_alluvial) > 16) {
  # If we have more than 16, prioritize top 12 by abundance, then add DA genera
  top_genera_alluvial <- c(
    top_genera_by_abundance,
    setdiff(da_genera_found, top_genera_by_abundance)
  )[1:min(16, length(top_genera_alluvial))]
}

# Filter to top genera and add "Other" category
# Use the grouped data (which has mean abundance per Genus × timepoint × carbohydrate)
# IMPORTANT: Use ALL data from alluvial_data_grouped (not filtered), so we preserve
# low-abundance combinations like RDC 0H
# Replace NaN with 0 before aggregating
alluvial_plot_data_pre_complete <- alluvial_data_grouped %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    mean_abundance = ifelse(is.nan(mean_abundance) | is.na(mean_abundance), 0, mean_abundance),
    Genus_grouped = ifelse(Genus %in% top_genera_alluvial, as.character(Genus), "Other")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Genus_grouped, timepoint, carbohydrate) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(Abundance = sum(mean_abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    Abundance = ifelse(is.nan(Abundance) | is.na(Abundance), 0, Abundance)
  )

# Ensure we have data for both timepoints for each carbohydrate AND all Genus_grouped values
alluvial_plot_data <- alluvial_plot_data_pre_complete %>%
  tidyr::complete(
    Genus_grouped = c(top_genera_alluvial, "Other"),
    timepoint = c("0H", "48H"),
    carbohydrate = c("No Added Carb", "RDC", "SDC"),
    fill = list(Abundance = 0)
  )

# Create color palette
genus_colors <- c(
  scico::scico(length(top_genera_alluvial), palette = "batlow"),
  "Other" = "grey80"
)
names(genus_colors)[1:length(top_genera_alluvial)] <- top_genera_alluvial

# Create alluvial plots for each carbohydrate
plot_list_alluvial <- list()

for (carb in c("No Added Carb", "RDC", "SDC")) {
  plot_data <- alluvial_plot_data %>%
    dplyr::filter(carbohydrate == carb)
  
  # Ensure both timepoints exist, even if one has zero abundance (fix for RDC panel)
  # Get all unique Genus_grouped values first
  all_genera <- unique(plot_data$Genus_grouped)
  plot_data <- plot_data %>%
    tidyr::complete(
      Genus_grouped = all_genera,
      timepoint = c("0H", "48H"),
      fill = list(Abundance = 0, carbohydrate = carb)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Genus_grouped = factor(
        Genus_grouped,
        levels = c(top_genera_alluvial[top_genera_alluvial %in% unique(Genus_grouped)], "Other")
      ),
      timepoint = factor(timepoint, levels = c("0H", "48H")),
      carbohydrate = carb
    )
  
  p <- ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(
      x = timepoint,
      y = Abundance,
      alluvium = Genus_grouped,
      stratum = Genus_grouped,
      fill = Genus_grouped
    )
  ) +
    geom_alluvium(alpha = 0.7, width = 0.3) +
    geom_stratum(width = 0.3, alpha = 0.9) +
    stat_stratum(
      geom = "text",
      aes(label = Genus_grouped),
      size = 2.3,
      fontface = "bold"
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = genus_colors) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.3, 0.3))) +
    labs(
      title = carb,
      x = "Timepoint",
      y = "Relative Abundance",
      fill = "Genus"
    ) +
    theme_scfa() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
    )
  
  plot_list_alluvial[[carb]] <- p
}

# Combine plots using patchwork
combined_alluvial <- wrap_plots(plot_list_alluvial, ncol = 3) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Genus Composition Changes from 0H to 48H by Carbohydrate Type",
    subtitle = paste0("Flow diagram showing relative abundance changes (top ", length(top_genera_alluvial), " genera including DA-important taxa)"),
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"))
  )

print(combined_alluvial)
```

```{r genus-validation, echo=FALSE, fig.width=14, fig.height=10, cache=FALSE}
# Extract genus-level data for validation bar plots

    by = "ASV"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(

  ) %>%

# Remove NA values to prevent NaN in calculations

  dplyr::filter(
    !is.na(Abundance),
    !is.na(Genus),
    !is.na(timepoint),
    !is.na(carbohydrate)
  )

# Calculate mean abundance per genus, timepoint, and carbohydrate
# Use ALL data first (don't filter yet) to preserve low-abundance combinations like RDC 0H
genus_summary_all <- genus_long_clean %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Genus, timepoint, carbohydrate) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean_abundance = mean(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE),
    se_abundance = sd(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
    n_samples = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Replace any NaN or NA with 0
    mean_abundance = ifelse(is.nan(mean_abundance) | is.na(mean_abundance), 0, mean_abundance),
    se_abundance = ifelse(is.nan(se_abundance) | is.na(se_abundance), 0, se_abundance)
  )

# Get top 15 genera overall (based on max abundance across all conditions)

  head(15) %>%

# Define genera that are important from DA analysis and should be included

# since taxonomy formats may vary (tax_table uses "g__" format)
da_important_genera <- c(
  "g_Fusicatenibacter",
  "g__Fusicatenibacter",
  "Fusicatenibacter",
  "g_Fusicatenibacters",
  "g__Fusicatenibacters",
  "Fusicatenibacters",
  "g_Hungatella",
  "g__Hungatella",
  "Hungatella",
  "g_Eggerthella",
  "g__Eggerthella",
  "Eggerthella",
  "g_Peptoniphilus",
  "g__Peptoniphilus",
  "Peptoniphilus"
)

# Check which of these genera exist in the data
# IMPORTANT: Get available_genera from the original tax_table, not from grouped data
# This ensures we find all genera in the taxonomy, even if they have zero/low abundance
available_genera_from_tax <- unique(tax_df$Genus)
available_genera_grouped <- unique(genus_summary_all$Genus)

# Check exact matches first
da_genera_in_data <- da_important_genera[da_important_genera %in% available_genera_from_tax]

# Also check for variations in the full taxonomy (e.g., "g__Fusicatenibacter sp." might be stored differently)
# This will catch any genus containing these names, regardless of prefix or suffix
da_genera_variations <- available_genera_from_tax[
  stringr::str_detect(available_genera_from_tax, regex("Fusicatenibacter|Hungatella|Eggerthella|Peptoniphilus", ignore_case = TRUE))
]

# Combine exact matches and variations
da_genera_found <- unique(c(da_genera_in_data, da_genera_variations))

# Combine top 15 by abundance with DA-important genera
# Remove duplicates and keep up to 19 genera total (15 + up to 4 DA genera)
```
